walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermodynamics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Thermodynamics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Thermodynamics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which best describes the second law of thermodynamics?
options: Energy is conserved in any process.
The total entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
Heat flows spontaneously from cold to hot.
Work and heat are equivalent forms of energy.

mcqs.q: A heat engine operates between 500 K and 300 K. Its maximum theoretical efficiency is:
Was the Big Bang an explosion of matter into pre-existing space?
options: No — it was the expansion of space itself, beginning from a hot dense state; there was no 'outside' for matter to expand into.
Yes — it was a giant explosion at a point, and galaxies are still flying outwards from it.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.
Yes — it was a bomb-like event that destroyed an earlier universe.

mcqs.q: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Is it accelerating?
options: Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.
Only if it speeds up or slows down on the circle.
No — constant speed means no acceleration.
Yes — its direction is constantly changing, so its velocity changes; centripetal acceleration points toward the centre of the circle.
